::: {#sol-weight-decay-sweep}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
def weight_norm(net):
    # Euclidean norm of all the weights, leaving out the biases.
    weights = [p.flatten() for name, p in net.named_parameters() if "weight" in name]
    return torch.cat(weights).norm().item()


decay_rows = []
for weight_decay in [0, 0.1, 1, 10]:
    decay_net = make_net()
    decay_history, _ = fit(decay_net, weight_decay=weight_decay)
    decay_rows.append({
        "weight_decay": weight_decay,
        "train_loss": decay_history["train"].iloc[-1],
        "val_loss": decay_history["val"].iloc[-1],
        "weight_norm": weight_norm(decay_net),
    })
decay_table = pd.DataFrame(decay_rows)
best_decay = decay_table.loc[decay_table["val_loss"].idxmin()]
print(decay_table.round(4))
```

`weight_decay` $= `r py$best_decay[["weight_decay"]]`$ ends with the lowest validation loss,
`r sprintf("%.3f", py$best_decay[["val_loss"]])`,
against `r sprintf("%.3f", py$decay_table$val_loss[1])` with no weight decay.
Weight decay keeps the weights smaller:
their norm after 300 [epochs](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/gradient-descent.html#def-epoch) falls from `r sprintf("%.1f", py$decay_table$weight_norm[1])` with no weight decay
to `r sprintf("%.1f", py$decay_table$weight_norm[4])` with `weight_decay` $= 10$.
At 10 the network no longer fits even its training images closely:
its training loss is `r sprintf("%.3f", py$decay_table$train_loss[4])`,
against `r sprintf("%.1e", py$decay_table$train_loss[1])` with no weight decay.

:::
